title: Mental rotation of 3-D objects
summary: Does judging whether two drawings show the same 3-D object take longer the further one is turned? Two drawings of cube objects, 0 to 180 degrees apart in depth or in the picture plane, are judged same or mirror image with a key. Measure: reaction time of correct 'same' answers against angle.
references: Shepard, R. N., & Metzler, J. (1971). Mental rotation of three-dimensional objects. Science, 171(3972), 701-703. doi:10.1126/science.171.3972.701

deviations.original: Line drawings reproduced by photo-offset on cards, seen through two circular apertures in a vertical black surface at about 60 cm
deviations.here: A computer display: the black surface and the two apertures are drawn, each aperture showing one image of the stimulus bank; sizes are set in degrees of visual angle from the rig file
deviations.reason: Cards cannot be presented by software; the visual angles the paper gives (9 deg spacing, 4-5 cm drawings at about 60 cm) are kept

deviations.original: Ten specific shapes (Fig. 1) drawn by a Bell Laboratories program
deviations.here: Ten shapes generated under the paper's stated constraints (10 cubes, 3 right-angled elbows, two mirror-image sets of five with no self- or cross-congruence within a set), picked by a fixed seed
deviations.reason: The original shape set is not given in the paper and its drawings are not redistributable; the constraints are

deviations.original: Perspective projections plotted on a Stromberg-Carlson 4020 microfilm recorder
deviations.here: Perspective projections with hidden lines removed, rendered by the folder's own rasterizer (numpy) as anti-aliased 512-px images; picture-plane rotations are the image turned on screen (interpolated)
deviations.reason: Reproducible and redistributable stimuli generated by a script in the folder

deviations.original: Pull a right-hand lever for "same", a left-hand lever for "different"
deviations.here: Press J (right hand) for "same", F (left hand) for "different" on a keyboard
deviations.reason: A keyboard is what a standard rig has; the hand assignment is the paper's

deviations.original: A warning tone, the pair half a second later
deviations.here: A small white dot between the apertures for the half second before the pair
deviations.reason: alhazen v3.6.0 sounds tones only for trial feedback; it has no tone bound to an arbitrary task event yet, and faking one with the feedback beep would mislabel the event

deviations.original: An electric timer started with the pair and stopped by the lever
deviations.here: RT from the display flip that showed the pair to the frame on which the key was read (resolution one frame, about 17 ms at 60 Hz, plus keyboard latency)
deviations.reason: Software timing on a frame-locked display

deviations.original: The black surface stayed in place while the cards were changed
deviations.here: After each answer alhazen blanks the window to its mid-grey background for the moment it takes to save the trial, then the black surface returns for the inter-trial interval
deviations.reason: alhazen's trial engine ends every trial with a blank flip in the window colour; the black surface is part of each trial

assumed.value: 4.3 deg (4.5 cm at 60 cm) as the mean maximum linear extent of all 70 drawings, one scale for all
assumed.reason: The paper gives a range: drawings averaged between 4 and 5 cm at about 60 cm (p. 703); the midpoint is taken

assumed.value: 6.0 deg
assumed.reason: Not stated; large enough for every drawing at any picture-plane rotation, leaving 3 deg between the apertures at the paper's 9 deg spacing

assumed.value: 0.04 deg (about 0.4 mm at 60 cm)
assumed.reason: Not stated; a thin pen line, legible at the drawing size

assumed.value: White disc at the display's maximum, black lines at its minimum
assumed.reason: Fig. 1 shows black line drawings in white circles; luminances are not stated

assumed.value: White dot, 0.3 deg, centred between the apertures for the 0.5 s before the pair, off at pair onset
assumed.reason: Stands in for the warning tone (see Deviations); size and place are a convention

assumed.value: 1.5 s of the black surface with empty apertures before each warning
assumed.reason: The paper's cards were changed by hand; no interval is given

assumed.value: 30 s; an unanswered pair is served again at the end of the block
assumed.reason: No deadline is described (mean RTs were 1-6 s); a deadline keeps a session from stalling

assumed.value: J
assumed.reason: The paper's right-hand lever meant "same" (p. 702); J is the right index finger's home key

assumed.value: F
assumed.reason: The left-hand lever meant "different" (p. 702); F is the left index finger's home key

assumed.value: Every straight run spans at least 2 cube steps (runs of 2, 2, 2 and 3 steps in some order)
assumed.reason: The paper says only 'armlike' with three elbows; shorter runs make stubs rather than arms

assumed.value: Seeded pick (seed 1971) from the 24 arms that qualify, keeping those with a valid set of seven views
assumed.reason: The originals are not reproducible; a fixed seed makes the set reproducible

assumed.value: Each shape stands in one of the 24 axis-aligned orientations (seeded), its cube edges vertical, and turns about the vertical axis through its centroid
assumed.reason: Not stated; Fig. 1's drawings have vertical cube edges and turn about the vertical axis

assumed.value: Azimuth 10 deg from the cube faces (views at 10, 30, ..., 350 deg)
assumed.reason: Not stated; with this offset the mirror object's views fall on the same 18 azimuths

assumed.value: 25 deg above the horizontal
assumed.reason: Not stated; the drawings look down on the objects (Fig. 1)

assumed.value: 25 cube edges (about five times the object's size): mild perspective
assumed.reason: Not stated; the projections are perspective (p. 702)

assumed.value: A view qualifies only if every cube shows at least 20% of its unoccluded front-face area
assumed.reason: The paper avoids views in which 'some part of the object was wholly occluded' without a criterion; per-cube visibility is a strict reading

assumed.value: Views straight onto the cube faces (azimuth 90 or 270 deg) are not used
assumed.reason: Accidental views in which edges coincide; the paper's figures show none

assumed.value: The 7-view set whose least visible cube is most visible (ties: lowest view indices)
assumed.reason: Several sets meet the paper's two conditions; a deterministic rule

assumed.value: 2 per object, type and angle (10 objects x 2 = the paper's 20)
assumed.reason: The paper gives 20 unique depth and 20 picture-plane pairs per angle, not how they divide among objects

assumed.value: Seeded random choice among the view pairs (depth) or views (picture plane) of the object at that angle; random left-right placement
assumed.reason: Not stated

assumed.value: One copy at its generated orientation, the other turned by the angle, clockwise or counterclockwise at random, on a random side
assumed.reason: The paper says only that the two copies differ in orientation by the angle (p. 702)

assumed.item: The reflected object in a "different" pair
assumed.value: One drawing, on a random side, replaced by the mirror object seen from the mirrored azimuth (a reflection through the vertical plane of the line of sight); the other drawing and both orientations kept
assumed.reason: The paper says one object was 'reflected about some plane in three-dimensional space' (p. 702)

assumed.value: 2 pure-depth, 2 pure-picture-plane and 4 mixed blocks of 200; each unique pair once in a pure and once in a mixed block
assumed.reason: The paper says blocks were pure or mixed, not how many of each

assumed.value: Every block balanced for rotation type, same/different and angle; random order within a block; random block order per subject
assumed.reason: The paper says only 'according to a random sequence'

assumed.value: 8 sessions, one 200-trial block each; the block order is fixed per subject id
assumed.reason: The paper: blocks of not more than 200 over eight to ten one-hour sessions (p. 702)

assumed.value: Each drawing centred on its bounding-box centre in its aperture; picture-plane rotation about the aperture centre
assumed.reason: Not stated

assumed.value: No feedback after a trial; no practice trials
assumed.reason: The paper describes neither

assumed.value: instructions.md
assumed.reason: The paper gives only the task, the levers and 'respond as quickly as possible while keeping errors to a minimum' (p. 703); the rest of the wording is ours

tasks.title: Mental rotation: same or different?
tasks.summary: Inter-trial interval on the black surface, a 0.5 s warning, then the pair until a key: J same, F different. RT runs from the pair's onset.

parameters.name: spacing_dva
parameters.label: Aperture spacing
parameters.meaning: Centre-to-centre distance of the two apertures.

parameters.name: drawing_extent_dva
parameters.label: Drawing size
parameters.meaning: Mean maximum linear extent of the 70 drawings. The paper gives 4-5 cm at about 60 cm; the midpoint is ASSUMED.

parameters.name: aperture_dva
parameters.label: Aperture diameter
parameters.meaning: Diameter of each circular aperture. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: line_width_dva
parameters.label: Line width
parameters.meaning: Width of the drawings' lines. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: warning_dot_dva
parameters.label: Warning dot
parameters.meaning: The visual warning signal that replaces the paper's tone (a deviation); its size is ASSUMED.

parameters.name: warning_duration
parameters.label: Warning to pair
parameters.meaning: From the warning to the pair's onset.

parameters.name: intertrial_interval
parameters.label: Inter-trial interval
parameters.meaning: Black surface with empty apertures before each warning. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: response_timeout
parameters.label: Response deadline
parameters.meaning: An unanswered pair ends here and is served again at the end of the block. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: same_key
parameters.label: Same key
parameters.meaning: Right hand, as the paper's right-hand lever meant 'same'. The letter is ASSUMED.

parameters.name: different_key
parameters.label: Different key
parameters.meaning: Left hand, as the paper's left-hand lever meant 'different'. The letter is ASSUMED.

parameters.name: objects.n_cubes
parameters.label: Cubes per object
parameters.meaning: Solid cubes attached face to face.

parameters.name: objects.n_elbows
parameters.label: Elbows
parameters.meaning: Right-angled elbows in each arm.

parameters.name: objects.n_views
parameters.label: Views per object
parameters.meaning: Perspective projections, one full turn about the vertical axis.

parameters.name: objects.views_per_object
parameters.label: Views kept
parameters.meaning: Views kept per object (70 drawings).

parameters.name: objects.elevation_deg
parameters.label: Camera elevation
parameters.meaning: Camera elevation above the horizontal. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: objects.min_visible_fraction
parameters.label: Occlusion rule
parameters.meaning: Every cube must show at least this fraction of its unoccluded front-face area. ASSUMED numeric form of the paper's rule.

parameters.name: design.angle_step_deg
parameters.label: Angle step
parameters.meaning: Angular differences 0 to 180 in this step.

parameters.name: design.presentations
parameters.label: Presentations per pair
parameters.meaning: Each unique pair is shown this many times.

parameters.name: design.block_size
parameters.label: Block size
parameters.meaning: Trials per block (the paper: not more than 200).

parameters.name: design.n_sessions
parameters.label: Sessions
parameters.meaning: One block per session; --ses picks it. ASSUMED (the paper: eight to ten sessions).

parameters.name: design.rehearsal_trials
parameters.label: Rehearsal sample
parameters.meaning: null in a real session; a number runs a stratified sample of the whole design (rehearsal only).

outcomes.name: CORRECT
outcomes.meaning: The key matched the pair: J for a 'same' pair, F for a 'different' pair.

outcomes.name: WRONG
outcomes.meaning: The other key. Kept (the paper analyses only correct RTs but reports the error rate).

outcomes.name: NO_RESPONSE
outcomes.meaning: No key before the deadline; the pair is served again at the end of the block.

events.name: ITI_ON
events.meaning: Black surface with empty apertures (inter-trial interval).

events.name: WARNING_ON
events.meaning: Warning dot shown; the pair follows 0.5 s later.

events.name: PAIR_ON
events.meaning: The pair shown; reaction time runs from this flip.

events.name: RESPONSE
events.meaning: The subject's key; the pair goes off.

tasks.timeline: ITI_ON (1.5 s) -> WARNING_ON (0.5 s) -> PAIR_ON -> RESPONSE
